status: in progress; requested throughput and memory parity not achieved
implementation: Published quinn-proto 0.11.19 plus narrow SparseMap patch. Unused remote stream credits retain their logical presence as inline ranges. Mutable access materializes a map entry. Transport parameter updates visit initialized state only. Advertised credits, flow-control windows, framing, congestion control and crypto rules are unchanged. Active stream lookup checks initialized state first.
scope: Local Linux loopback; same application and frozen maintained verifier. Three alternating fresh-process repetitions per variant/case, four pinned server I/O workers on CPUs 0-3 and eight pinned client workers on CPUs 8-15. Four-second saturation, 1 KiB values, 32 private pairs, 1024 room readers with fanout window four. Exact content, sender, FIFO, counters, departures, close/EOF or genuine close ACK, and cleanup checked. Logarithmic percentile values are upper bounds, not exact quantiles. RSS is sampled at gates, excludes kernel socket memory, and is not requested live heap or continuous peak. Higher post-retirement RSS is recorded explicitly; zero logical gauges do not prove RSS returned to the OS.

validation.quinn_protocol_scope: Standalone published-crate copy with all three modified source files byte-identical to the vendored candidate. Includes two new map tests and the original protocol tests. Root Cargo cannot run a non-workspace dependency package with dev-dependencies; standalone copy avoids mutating vendored archive metadata.
validation.vendor: 121 files checked against 3 original archive checksums and 2 declared patches
validation.browser: Chromium 155 passed all 9 actual delivered-bundle checks, including typed values, cross-room private/broadcast, datagrams, 128 KiB and 5 MiB payloads, concurrent variables, departure and graceful close. Seven connection/storage gauges zero after close.

heap.scope: 8194 sessions; gperftools replacement allocator; requested live bytes at ready gate, not ordinary RSS/timings. Prototype sparse implementation has same data layout; final active-lookup revision is separately benchmarked without instrumentation.

layout.scope: Public types compiled against the candidate library; full source and build-library association in artifacts/webtransport/quinn-layout.rs and quinn-sparse-active-build.jsonl. These sizes alone do not establish retained allocation causation.
layout.next_work: Profile the connection event channel and application task retention, along with mixed private/fanout scheduling. Do not reduce stream credits to claim a memory win.

diagnostics.initial_sparse_trial: The first map version consulted deferred ranges on each mutable lookup. Its two-run medians were about 4% lower for private traffic with large control variation; receipts quinn-sparse-*.json and v1 patch retained. Final map checks initialized state first and uses three alternating repetitions per case. Private and room medians remain about 1% below control; mixed is effectively unchanged, so this is a memory improvement without a throughput-gain claim.

freshness_scope: One candidate regression sample per mode/profile, 360 prepared 1 KiB states at 60 Hz for six seconds with reliable 1 MiB bulk. Clean; 20 ms one-way delay plus 2% loss; then also 8 ms jitter and 25% reordering. External transport port only in temporary isolated namespace, both directions. TLS proxy internal hop unimpaired. Identical parameters/seeds are not identical packet-loss trajectories. Newest-state probes include the initial period before the first state; stale datagrams cannot replace newer state. Missing means unreceived in observation window, not exclusively attributed network loss. No statistically established cross-protocol ranking from single runs.
remaining: Overall acceptance remains unproven: memory is still far above the fresh plaintext control, room/mixed throughput trails plaintext, private traffic under fanout trails the encrypted fixture. Observer cancellation/re-subscribe acceptance, full concurrent 100k/8192 inspection workload, broader overload/shutdown acceptance, QUIC buffer accounting and final packaging/deployment documentation remain outstanding.
